title: Emberlane concurrency & SLA discovery - hosted/dedicated/private evaluation
transcript:
00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about an hour, quick intros, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Evan's our SE and Noah's on CS.
00:18 Riley (Emberlane): Hey Maya, thanks — Riley here. Quick note, we spilled coffee so apologies if I'm a bit slow.
00:25 Priya (Emberlane): Priya, ML lead — we'll mostly ask about latency and burst.
00:32 Maya: Great, quick agenda: current stack, p95 targets, concurrency patterns, streaming vs batch, hosted vs dedicated vs private, next steps.
00:42 Evan (Redwood SE): I'll lean into latency numbers and how our runtime and routing works.
00:48 Sam (Emberlane): I'm infra, I care about VPC, network egress, KMS, and certs.
01:05 Maya: Startup context — Emberlane is building an AI assistant in your product for customer support, heavy streaming, expected concurrency pattern: mid-week spikes 200-400 active streams, baseline 40-60. Peak token/sec rates per user about 30-70 tokens/sec while streaming long responses. Correct?
01:22 Priya: That's right. We also have some batch scoring jobs but main pain is real-time streaming and maintaining p95 for first token and subsequent tokens.
01:36 Evan: When you say p95, is that per-token latency or per-response completion p95?
01:42 Priya: Both. We want p95 first token < 300ms and steady-state token latency such that generation keeps up around 20-40ms per token ideally, and overall completion p95 under 1.2s for typical 64-token responses.
02:00 Maya: Okay, very helpful. Are you leaning Hosted first or do you require Private right away?
02:07 Riley: Security is important, but we can start Hosted for a pilot if data masking is OK. However, we're evaluating Dedicated and Private for long term. Air-gap is not required but we need SOC 2, SSO, and audit logs.
02:21 Evan: Redwood Hosted supports SOC2 and SSO/SAML, we can share the SOC2 report — we'll add the link in next steps.
02:30 Sam: For Dedicated/Private — we need to run in our VPC, KMS integration for customer keys and HSM access for token encryption. How does Redwood handle KMS in Private?
02:45 Evan: In Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and can restrict egress.
02:55 Priya: Ok cool. On perf side — what's typical p95 for a 13B open model you host, for streaming at 50 concurrent steams?
03:07 Evan: Depends on hardware and quantization. On an A100-like fleet with optimized kernels and continuous batching, p95 first-token often 120-260ms for small prompts; streaming token steady-state p95 can be 18-45ms/token. But in hosted multi-tenant mode those numbers vary with burst. For Dedicated, you get more consistent p95.
03:33 Riley: Do you have concrete numbers we can use for capacity planning? We need to size for 99th-percentile concurrency across peak windows.
03:42 Maya: We have a perf_matrix.xlsx — it maps tokens/sec and concurrency to GPU pool sizes and back-of-envelope cost. We'll share. Also we can run a trial benchmark with your prompts on a dedicated pool.
03:55 Priya: That'd be ideal. How do you handle prefix/KV cache for chat histories? Our chat windows are long and we reuse context a lot.
04:06 Evan: We support KV cache and prefix caching. For repeated contexts we can keep warm caches on the serving nodes which improves p95 by avoiding serialization overhead. For Dedicated/Private we can pin caches to nodes to optimize locality.
04:24 Sam: Any guidance on batching and effect on token latency? We can't batch across users if we need immediate streaming.
04:32 Evan: There's continuous microbatching in the runtime that preserves streaming semantics — the system tries to batch tokens that arrive within a small window (10-40ms) if it helps throughput without harming latency SLOs. You can configure stricter latency policy to prefer single-request execution.
04:50 Priya: We'll need to experiment — sometimes we prefer slight latency increase for cost savings. We want to be able to toggle quantization profiles per-route.
04:59 Evan: Absolutely — Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload and per-model. You can route lower-cost quantized variants for low criticality paths and full-precision for important flows.
05:12 Riley: On routing — if a Dedicated pool is saturated, do you spill to Hosted? We need to avoid leaking PII to hosted if we run in Private.
05:22 Evan: Routing is policy-driven. You can set a no-egress policy for Private; for Dedicated we can configure fallback to a compatible private variant or queue. If you allow spill to Redwood Hosted, we can also enforce redaction and retention policies.
05:36 Maya: Any questions about SLAs?
05:39 Sam: We're eyeing p95 latency SLA of 500ms for interactive features and 99.9% uptime. What does Dedicated SLA look like?
05:48 Evan: Dedicated has SLA options with uptime and throughput guarantees tied to reserved capacity. We can also offer canary rollouts and automatic fallback. For strict p95 latency guarantees we usually size with buffer and define burst capacity.
06:03 Priya: Can Redwood run our exact prompt set for benchmarking? We want realistic numbers not synthetic ones.
06:10 Evan: Yes, we'll sign an NDA if needed and run your prompt corpus through our benchmark harness on a shared or dedicated pool. That gives p50/p95/p99 breakdown and token/sec numbers.
06:23 Riley: Cost — rough order of magnitude for Dedicated pool that handles 300 concurrent streaming sessions at 40 tokens/sec steady-state?
06:34 Maya: We'll run numbers but expect that Dedicated is more expensive than multi-tenant per-token but gives predictable latency and avoids noisy neighbors — we'll return a model in the perf spreadsheet.
06:46 Sam: We need to understand tokenization variance too — we use mixed content with code blocks and base64 attachments sometimes. That can spike token counts.
06:58 Priya: Also, what about warm-up and cold-start behavior? During nightly deploys we can't have long cold tails.
07:06 Evan: Warm pools and pre-warmed kernels reduce cold-start to seconds. We also offer rolling restarts and pinned models to avoid warm-down.
07:18 Riley: Any security red flags?
07:20 Maya: We'll send SOC2, network diagram, and the compliance pack.
07:24 Priya: Good. Can we get performance numbers by model family? For instance, 7B quantized vs 13B quantized vs 70B inf?
07:33 Evan: Yes — we can show throughput and steady-state tokens/sec for each. Typically 7B quantized may give 2-3x token/sec versus 13B but quality differs. 70B will be slower. We'll include recommended quantization profiles.
07:50 Sam: How about telemetry and observability? We want token-level cost, per-route latency, and tracing across our services.
07:59 Noah (CS): Console exposes per-route dashboards, token and cost breakdowns, p95 latencies, and you can ship traces; retention tiers are configurable.
08:12 Priya: Alerts on regressions tied to eval prompt sets — can Redwood hook evals to signal quality drops?
08:20 Evan: Yes, Redwood Optimize has quality monitors that run your eval prompts and trigger alerts if similarity or score drops beyond thresholds.
08:30 Riley: Ok next steps?
08:32 Maya: Recap — share SOC2 and network diagram, send perf_matrix.xlsx, set up NDA and benchmarking job, schedule technical deep dive for infra team for private deployment details.
08:45 Priya: Timeline — we want a pilot in 2-3 weeks and decision end of Q2.
08:52 Maya: Noted.
09:00 -- Transcript continues with clarifications and side conversations --
15:12 Priya: random mis-transcription sometimes says K-V cache as KV-Cache or K V, we get that in other transcripts.
15:22 Evan: yeah the auto transcript can flip acronyms, sorry.
20:03 Riley: On burst, can we get burst capacity multipliers for 5x baseline?
20:09 Maya: Yes — Dedicated can configure autoscale and short-term burst. We'll add numbers in the spreadsheet.
25:00 Sam: Our compliance requires audit logs for 18 months, is that achievable?
25:06 Noah: Yes, we have add-on options for longer retention.
30:12 Priya: A note on model pinning — if we pin to a specific model version will Redwood still push security patches?
30:20 Evan: Patches at infra and runtime are separate; model weights/versioning is yours to pin. We manage runtime patches and can notify you before upgrades.
35:00 Maya: Closing: we'll circulate notes, attach links to SOC2 and perf matrix, and Evan will schedule the infra deep dive.
35:15 Riley: Thanks, that was helpful.
35:20 End of recording.
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency and streaming throughput for an AI assistant use case. Emberlane is evaluating starting hosted pilot with move to Dedicated or Private for compliance. Key asks: p95 first token < 300ms, steady-state token latency targets, concurrency up to ~400 peak, KV/prefix caching behavior, KMS/HSM and VPC integration, dedicated sizing and burst configs, and benchmark on customer prompts.

Noah: Provide SOC2 report and compliance pack (due 2027-02-11)
Evan: Schedule infra deep dive meeting for Private deployment (due 2027-02-17)
Evan: Run initial benchmark on sample prompt set after NDA (due 2027-02-18)
Priya: Send sample prompt corpus and tokenization edge cases (due 2027-02-11)

Execute NDA and run customer-prompt benchmark on dedicated pool
Follow-up technical deep dive for private deployment (VPC/KMS/HSM)
